skill.name: iotnet
skill.description: Analyze IoT packet captures and live traffic with IoTNet to identify protocols, insecure communications, weak authentication, and other network security concerns.
skill.summary: Guide IoTNet traffic analysis and turn packet data into prioritized IoT security findings.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most reported shell-execution patterns are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline parameter names. Four sudo instructions are confirmed because live capture runs IoTNet with elevated privileges, and the workflow lacks explicit authorization and privacy safeguards for inspecting network traffic.

remediation.issue: Live capture examples invoke IoTNet through sudo.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before elevation and document a least-privilege capture setup using restricted capabilities or a dedicated capture group.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not verify authorization before capturing traffic that may contain credentials or private communications.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmed ownership or written permission, define capture scope and duration, and redact sensitive payloads from reports.

remediation.issue: File paths, interfaces, IP addresses, and filter expressions may originate from user input.
remediation.suggestion: Validate each argument against its expected format, pass arguments without shell concatenation, and reject unsupported filter syntax.

content.user_title: Analyze IoT Network Traffic for Security Risks
content.value_statement: IoT packet captures can hide insecure protocols, plaintext data, and weak authentication. This skill guides IoTNet analysis and presents prioritized findings with remediation advice.
actual_capabilities: Analyze one or more PCAP files with IoTNet.
Guide live capture by network interface, duration, and BPF filter.
Filter analysis by IP address or Wireshark display expression.
Identify IoT protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, ONVIF, UPnP, and Modbus.
Summarize protocol distribution, vulnerabilities, severity, packet details, and remediation recommendations.
limitations: IoTNet must already be installed and available from the iothackbot bin directory.
Live capture requires elevated privileges and access to the selected network interface.
The skill guides command usage but does not install dependencies or configure capture permissions.
Detection depends on configured rules and does not prove that a reported issue is exploitable.

use_cases.title: Review Device Captures
use_cases.description: Analyze authorized PCAP files to identify IoT protocols, plaintext traffic, and weak authentication.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Communications
use_cases.description: Compare device traffic against encryption and authentication requirements before a release.

use_cases.title: Triage Network Findings
use_cases.description: Summarize protocol distribution and prioritize likely communication risks for remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [PCAP path] with IoTNet. Identify IoT protocols and summarize security findings by severity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with an authorized packet capture.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on One Device
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [PCAP path] for traffic involving [device IP]. Report insecure protocols, missing encryption, and weak authentication.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate an authorized device within a larger capture.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Captures
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [PCAP paths] with [rules file]. Compare protocol distribution, security findings, and remediation priorities across captures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate several device tests with custom detection rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Scoped Live Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized live capture on [interface] for [duration] using [BPF filter]. Confirm scope and privilege requirements before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a controlled capture with explicit authorization.

output_examples.input: Analyze office-floor.pcap for IoT protocols and security issues.
output_examples.output: IoTNet identified MQTT and CoAP traffic. The highest priority finding is unencrypted MQTT communication that may expose device messages.

output_examples.input: Compare baseline.pcap and updated.pcap using the custom detection rules.
output: The updated capture contains less plaintext MQTT traffic than the baseline.
CoAP traffic remains unencrypted and requires review.
Prioritize transport encryption, then verify device authentication.

output_examples.input: Review camera.pcap for traffic from the authorized camera address.
output_examples.output: The filtered capture contains ONVIF and UPnP traffic. Review exposed discovery messages and verify that camera management traffic uses protected transport.

best_practices: Confirm network ownership or written authorization before analyzing or capturing traffic.
Prefer offline PCAP analysis when live capture is unnecessary.
Limit capture scope and redact credentials or sensitive payloads from shared results.
anti_patterns: Do not capture third-party traffic without explicit permission.
Do not run broad or indefinite live captures with elevated privileges.
Do not treat protocol detection alone as proof of a vulnerability.

faq.question: Can this skill analyze existing packet captures?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports one or more standard PCAP files and does not require elevated privileges for offline analysis.

faq.question: Can it capture live traffic?
faq.answer: Yes. Live capture requires an interface, a duration, network access, explicit authorization, and elevated capture permissions.

faq.question: Which IoT protocols can it identify?
faq.answer: Documented examples include MQTT, CoAP, Zigbee, Z-Wave, ONVIF, UPnP, SSDP, and Modbus.

faq.question: Can I filter the analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. You can filter by IP address, BPF capture expression, or Wireshark display expression.

faq.question: Does it support custom detection rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a custom rules configuration file through the documented config option.

faq.question: Does a finding confirm that a device is vulnerable?
faq.answer: No. Findings require validation against device configuration, deployment context, and authorized testing results.
